exposure: nutritional status (24-hour food consumption, anthropometric measurements, dietary preferences)
cohort: The study included 58 participants aged 3-15 years diagnosed with cerebral palsy.
finding: Children with epilepsy demonstrated dietary preferences that were higher in energy, carbohydrates, and saturated fats, and showed signs of malnutrition and increased chewing/swallowing difficulties.
mod_finding: Children born via cesarean section had a significantly higher risk of epileptic seizures compared to those born via vaginal delivery.
